title: optimistic-handoff-orchestrator-kernel-affinity-routing-and-early-commit-metrics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement an optimistic handoff orchestrator that routes decode work to a fast-path model/kernel combination when early-commit confidence signals are observed, and gracefully falls back to the canonical slow-path when signals are insufficient. This work spans kernel affinity (selecting GPU kernel variants based on attention profile), lightweight attention-sparsity hints during prefill, an early-commit confidence curve (ECC) metric to drive accept/reject decisions, and a fallback/soft-retract plan with SLO guardrails. The orchestrator will be pluggable in the runtime's router layer and expose telemetry for analysis and rollout control.
acceptance_criteria: Fast-path routing: requests that meet ECC thresholds are routed to optimized kernel/model variants and show >=20% p95 latency improvement on target workloads
Fallback correctness: any fast-path that fails acceptance is retried on slow-path without loss of tokens or double-charging; fallbacks must not increase application-visible error rate
Observable metrics: new telemetry (early_commit_rate, retract_rate, delta_entropy_histogram, model_fallback_rate) is emitted and available on the runtime dashboard
Controlled rollout: feature flag + gradual traffic ramp (0 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100%) with automatic rollback on defined safety triggers
implementation_notes: Architecture: add an OptimisticHandoff module that registers a kernel-affinity predictor and a lightweight ECC evaluator. The predictor consumes prefill attention summaries (max-attention-span, average-attention-sparsity) and model metadata to pick a kernel variant. ECC is computed as a rolling confidence delta over the first N decode steps (N configurable, default 4). If ECC >= threshold, commit tokens from fast-path; if ECC drops under soft-margin, trigger soft-retract and enqueue slow-path rollout. Key considerations: ensure KV cache consistency, avoid duplicate token emission, and keep cost accounting deterministic. Use fast atomic switches in scheduler to avoid head-of-line blocking. Add feature flag gates and a canary-scoped router policy for experiments.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): feature flag on in eu-west region for 1% of traffic for low-risk customers for 72h. Monitor early_commit_rate, retract_rate, p95 latency, and errors. Phase 2: increase to 10% if retract_rate < 0.5% and no customer errors. Phase 3: 50% with automated throttling; Phase 4: global enable. Automatic rollback if fastpath_error_rate > 0.1% or p95 latency regresses >5% for 30m.
fallback_plan: Soft-retract: when ECC dips below soft_margin, pause committing fast-path tokens and fire a synchronized slow-path decode using the same model version. On slow-path success, emit a retract event and replace fast-path output. Ensure KV caches are reconciled by applying slow-path KV delta. If KV reconciliation fails, trigger circuit-breaker and route remaining requests to conservative model-tier.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: token duplication between fast and slow path -> Mitigation: idempotent commit envelopes and sequence stamps
Risk: expensive fallbacks raising cost -> Mitigation: conservative ECC thresholds and per-customer cost caps
Risk: kernel mismatch causing incorrect outputs -> Mitigation: kernel compatibility table and unit tests for attention-edge cases
Risk: observability blind spots -> Mitigation: instrument delta-entropy and kv-cache diagnostics prior to rollout
